**CLAIM** — session `session_017Qqyix2QcnpUC9XeYVDzx3`, branch `claude/issue-4580-one-schemanode`. This seat absorbs #4581 (same producer surface, same canary — landing them separately would run the repo-wide type canary twice for one reconciliation).

**PM ruling (delegated, veto window open):** the spec of record is `packages/types`' union — `SchemaNode = BaseSchema | string | number | boolean | null | undefined`, whose doc comment already names plain strings as valid nodes and which #4548's canary measured as the side 19 of 35 collision errors resolve toward. `packages/core`'s `interface SchemaNode` (required `type` + index signature) becomes a re-export of types' declaration — core already depends on `@object-ui/types`, so the edge exists and adds no cycle. #4581 rides along: `BaseSchema.visible` widens to `boolean | string`, `ariaLabel` to `string | I18nLabel`, and the five commented `as unknown as BaseSchema` casts in the react/components test fixtures drop.

**Two things stay, stated so nobody cleans them up:** `toRenderableSchema` in `packages/react` remains — SchemaRenderer's component-level union deliberately excludes `number`/`boolean` (#4548 ruling, Q2), so the bridge still normalizes those even after reconciliation. And the gate's existing behavior around these names is #4592's card, not this one.

Mutual exclusion: PR #4589 is armed on `packages/core/src/index.ts` + `core/src/utils/**` + `packages/i18n/**` — merge `origin/main` forward when it lands; STOP and report if the canary demands source edits under `core/src/utils/**`. #4592 (also in flight) owns `scripts/` — don't touch the gates.

**PM step-7 复核: ACCEPT — the STOP was the ruling working as designed, and PR #4593 (the surviving half) is flipped and armed.**

复核 checked: #4593's four files match the report exactly (base.ts widening with evidence comment, invariant `Equal` pin with written-first predictions, honest cast-drop comments recording the `disabled` residue, changeset with the position analysis inline); emitted JS proven byte-identical by bundle sha256, meeting the types-only bar as proof rather than argument; CI converged 20/20. Withdrawing the verified SchemaNode reconciliation instead of "fixing" the two list-view.ts runtime errors it exposed was the correct execution of ruling 4 — the canary did its job: those two sites are a real vocabulary defect (`I18nLabel` flowing into `string` slots through core's index signature), not a mechanical narrowing.

**Rulings on the four open questions (delegated, veto windows open):**

- **Q1 — B, accepted in principle, premise-gated.** `BaseSchema.label`/`.description` stay `string`; the spec bridges resolve inline maps at the spec→schema boundary using the spec's OWN `resolveI18nLabel` (the resolver choice PR #4208 already established for this family), locale from the one display-locale channel. **Premise to verify before implementing:** the bridge's invocation context can know the locale AND re-translates on locale change — if measured otherwise, STOP and report the measured alternative. This is runtime work with its own red-first (the `[object Object]` harm on screen), not a types-only rider. C is rejected for the reason the report gives.
- **Q2 — B, accepted; my `string | I18nLabel` spelling in the original #4581 ruling is withdrawn as measured-wrong.** The three probe measurements (vacuous green on the keyed fixture, rejected `params`, empty aria-label on a genuine map) are decisive. `ariaLabel` declares the KEYED form, and the shape gets a name — `KeyedI18nLabel` in `@object-ui/types` — retiring the three inline copies rather than adding a fourth. C rejected: the two vocabularies are structurally confusable, which is #4167's exact hazard.
- **Q3 — A.** `disabled` widens to `boolean | string` with the same evidence shape as `visible`; the asymmetry was accidental, not deliberate. Folded into the same follow-up seat.
- **Q4 — B.** On re-dispatch, the bridges' return types are annotated `BaseSchema` where they provably return objects (type-annotation-only, inside the types-only carve-out), then the residue is narrowed. The withdrawn reconciliation pin (preserved by this seat) is the follow-up's red case.

**Sequencing:** one follow-up seat executes Q2+Q3+Q1 together (they share the vocabulary ruling and, after #4593 lands, a single owner of `base.ts`), closing #4581 fully and clearing #4580's blocker; #4580 is then re-dispatched with Q4-B. ⚠️ That seat must check PR #4208's pending diff (the rc.6 train, blocked on #4165) before touching `packages/layout` or `app-shell/utils` — no rebase conflicts for the train; an overlapping inline-copy retirement waits for the train instead.

#4594 (ComponentRendererProps dual declaration) noted as observation-class; the #4163 evidence comment is exactly where that belongs.

**PM ruling revision — Q1 (delegated; ⚠️ this veto window is a REAL one, not pro-forma: it reverses my own earlier Q1-B).**

PR #4603's seat measured Q1-B's premise false on every leg: the bridge is a plain class method that cannot call a hook, `BridgeContext` declares no locale, context is assigned once with `updateContext()` at zero callers (no re-translation channel), and `SpecBridge` has zero in-repo production consumers. Resolving at the bridge would bake one audience's language into the node tree — the exact defect class the spec's own resolver doc records (#6761). Q1-B is therefore unimplementable as ruled, and I am revising it rather than leaving the reconciliation permanently blocked:

**Revised Q1 ruling — option A: `BaseSchema.label` and `.description` widen to `string | I18nLabel`, and resolution happens at READ time in the renderer against `useDisplayLocale()`.**

- **Why A:** the locale lives where components live; React's own invalidation re-translates on locale change for free; and this is how every existing localized read site already works (ObjectDataTable, ObjectGantt, DatasetPreview — the #4163 Part-1 pattern, worked in PR #4208). The bridges then need NO change: `spec.label: I18nLabel` flows into `node.label: string | I18nLabel` legally, and both list-view.ts blockers die without touching the bridge.
- **Why not B** (BridgeContext gains a locale): builds an invalidation contract for a surface with zero measured consumers, and its failure mode — a host forgetting to re-transform, silently shipping one language to everyone — is unmitigable by types or tests. **Why not C**: it re-blocks the reconciliation forever and keeps the live defect (an authored `{ en: …, 'zh-CN': … }` renders as an object).
- **The confusability cost is real and accepted with mitigation:** one interface now carries both vocabularies two properties apart (`label`/`description` = spec's inline map; `ariaLabel` = keyed ref). The mitigation is exactly what PR #4603 bought — both shapes are NAMED with cross-referenced doc comments stating which resolver owns which slot. The hazard an author faces (a keyed ref typed into `label` vacuously accepted as a map) is the spec's own `I18nLabel` design hazard (#4167), present on every spec surface that uses it — not new to BaseSchema.
- **Mechanics for the executing seat:** the widening turns every blind `schema.label`-as-string read into a named TS2322 — that compiler-generated inventory IS the audit, same as the rc.6 bump produced #4163's 13-site list. Each named site resolves via the spec's `resolveI18nLabel` against the display locale, following PR #4208's conventions (including the layout package's no-i18n-dependency rule). #4603's `assertionLabel`/`assertionDescription` pins were written as the OLD ruling and turn red on purpose — they move to pin the widened unions, declared as `PIN MOVED`.

**Sequencing:** this rides the #4580 re-dispatch as ONE seat — label/description widening + read-site resolutions + the SchemaNode reconciliation (types' union wins, core re-exports) + Q4-B (bridge return types annotated `BaseSchema`, then residue narrowing) + the preserved reconciliation pin from PR #4593's seat. One repo-wide canary instead of two. Dispatches when PR #4603 lands.

**PM step-7 复核: ACCEPT — and this closes the whole SchemaNode / label-vocabulary family.** PR #4608 executes all three pieces with the proof discipline at full strength: the 4-site inventory (one class, far under the STOP threshold) with the REAL harm captured per site ("Objects are not valid as a React child" — a refused text node, not `[object Object]`, correctly distinguished) and the Radix lazy-mount vacuous-probe correction kept in the header; the preserved reconciliation pin restored byte-identical AND its latent load-order defect found, fixed, and re-proven non-vacuous (round 1 only ever type-checked it — this is why pins get re-run, not trusted); piece C's 272→0 with executable-code byte-identity; core's entry `.d.ts` byte-identical reproducing round 1; the honest canary note that main's collision was LATENT (the pin carries piece B's red, not a manufactured before-count); and the two bridge expressions proven untouched by selective revert rather than asserted.

**The site-4 deviation is ACCEPTED as measured-better.** Within a component that already resolves the SAME vocabulary on the sibling slot (`widget.title` via `pickLocalized(…, language)`), joining that channel is right: two resolvers and two locale channels in one component would let a heading and the titles beneath it disagree in one render, and `pickLocalized` is the parity-pinned limb-for-limb twin (objectstack#6765). Whether `DashboardGridLayout` as a whole should converge on `useDisplayLocale` is the existing one-channel family's question, not this card's — correctly left.

react's return-type narrowing flagged for BridgeFn implementers is the right honesty in the changeset. The stale `ui-action.ts` comment ("In spec 17 I18nLabelSchema is z.ZodString" — false, and it nearly turned this card into a no-op) is being filed as its own finding — it is the content-wrong-claim class the citation gate deliberately does not judge. #4605's census grows by label/description as noted.

Flipping ready and arming auto-merge now. `Fixes #4580` closes this card on landing.
